devote time to: to spend time doing or supporting something
Local volunteers devote time to teaching adults basic literacy.
epidemiologist: a scientist who studies the spread and causes of diseases
An epidemiologist examined how the infection spread through the town.
respiratory disease: an illness affecting the lungs or breathing passages
Air pollution can increase the risk of respiratory disease.
affordability: The quality of being affordable; the extent to which something is within one's financial means.
The affordability of housing is a major concern for young families in urban areas.
life-changing: having a major and lasting effect on someone's life
Access to clean water was life-changing for the remote community.
bustling: full of busy activity and movement
The bustling night market spills onto every street corner.
teem with: to be full of people, animals, or things
During spring, the wetlands teem with birds and insects.
din: The deafening din from the construction site disrupted classes throughout the entire morning.
go about one's daily lives: to carry on with ordinary everyday activities
Residents go about their daily lives despite the nearby construction.
overriding aim: the most important purpose guiding an activity
The overriding aim of the project is to improve public health.
low educational achievement: poor performance or limited success in education
Low educational achievement often reflects unequal access to resources.
drop out of: to leave a course or school before finishing it
Some students drop out of university because they cannot afford tuition.
disproportionately: to an extent that is too large or too small
Rural households are disproportionately affected by rising energy costs.
learning outcome: The main learning outcome of the unit is to write a short argument.
pupil-centred: focused on learners' needs, interests, and participation
lấy học sinh làm trung tâm
Pupil-centred lessons encourage children to ask questions and explore ideas.
medium of instruction: the language used to teach school subjects
The school chose English as its medium of instruction.
hold back: stop someone or something from moving forwards
ngăn chặn ai đó hoặc một cái gì đó di chuyển về phía trước
Police officers formed a barricade to hold back the advancing crowd of protesters.
exposure to: the state of being subjected to something
Regular exposure to books can strengthen children's reading skills.
socio-economic: relating to both social conditions and economic factors
Socio-economic conditions can shape a child's educational opportunities.
withdraw: to move back or remove oneself from a place or activity
Sadly, this can make them withdraw even further, creating a hard cycle to break.
that ship has sailed: the opportunity to do something has passed
We cannot apply for that grant now; that ship has sailed.
uniformity: the state of being the same in all parts or cases
Uniformity in building design gives the street a calm, orderly appearance.
tailor to: to adapt something for a particular person or purpose
Teachers tailor lessons to meet the needs of different learners.
lag behind: to make slower progress than others
Students without internet access may lag behind their classmates.
numeracy: the ability to understand and work with numbers
Basic numeracy skills are essential for everyday life and many jobs.
be down to: caused by or dependent on a particular factor or person
Her remarkable academic success may largely be down to her persistent hard work.
catch the attention of: to make someone notice or show interest in something
thu hút sự chú ý của
The striking cover design quickly managed to catch the attention of young readers.
inform (policy): to provide facts or knowledge that shape official decisions
định hình chính sách, làm cơ sở
New climate research will directly inform policy on renewable energy development nationwide.
deprivation: a lack of the things people need for a decent standard of living
Children from areas of deprivation often have fewer opportunities.
attenuate: to reduce the force, strength or effect of something
Wetlands can attenuate floodwaters before they reach nearby towns.
be doomed: certain to fail, suffer badly, or experience catastrophe
chắc chắn thất bại hoặc diệt vong
Without immediate financial support, the startup will be doomed to total failure.
to the detriment of: causing harm, damage, or loss to someone or something
gây tổn hại hoặc thiệt hại cho

bridge (a with b): to connect two different ideas or reduce differences between them
kết nối, thu hẹp khoảng cách
The new educational project helps bridge theory with practical classroom experience.
obsessive: She has an obsessive need to keep everything clean.
bespoke: made specially for a particular customer or purpose
đặt làm riêng, theo yêu cầu
The firm built a bespoke software platform for the hospital's needs.
impulsive: Acting quickly on feelings without thinking carefully about the results.
The impulsive boy jumped into the pool before anyone could stop him.
repressed: prevented from being expressed, acknowledged, or freely experienced
bị kìm nén, bị ức chế
Long periods of stress often lead to deeply repressed anger and anxiety.
stubbornly held: maintained firmly and refusing to change despite contradictory evidence
Scientists easily dismantled the stubbornly held beliefs regarding the ancient myth.
ignorance: lack of knowledge or information about something
His mistake was caused by ignorance rather than carelessness.
spherical: Raindrops typically assume a spherical shape as they fall through the Earth's atmosphere.
liken (a to b): to represent someone or something as similar to another
Philosophers often liken the human mind to an intricate, interconnected web.
shoddy: Consumers frequently complained about the shoddy craftsmanship of these imported household appliances.
bust one's budget: to spend much more money than planned or allocated
vượt quá ngân sách chi tiêu
Extravagant dining during vacations can easily bust one's budget in several days.
artisan: a skilled worker who makes things by hand, often in a traditional way
The village is famous for its artisans, who weave fine silk by hand.
draw a blank: to fail to recall information or find a desired solution
không nhớ ra, không có kết quả
I tried to recall her surname during the meeting but could only draw a blank.
thwart: to prevent someone from achieving a plan or goal
The police thwarted the plan to rob the bank on Friday night.
opt for: to decide on or choose a particular alternative
Many commuters currently opt for cycling instead of driving crowded private cars.
abortive: unsuccessful, failing to achieve the intended result
The rebels' abortive uprising ended within a single day.
prise: to force open or separate something using leverage
The burglar attempted to prise the metal lock open with a sturdy iron rod.
do the trick: to achieve the necessary or intended result successfully
giải quyết được vấn đề, hiệu quả
A hot cup of herbal tea should do the trick for your persistent cough.
seep out: to leak or escape slowly through tiny cracks or openings
rò rỉ, thấm rỉ ra ngoài
Hazardous chemicals began to seep out from the damaged industrial storage tank.
painstaking: Done with great care and effort, usually over a long time.
công phu, tốn nhiều công sức
Restoring the damaged manuscript was painstaking work: experts spent weeks repairing a single page.
palpable: so strong or intense that it can be easily felt
rõ ràng, có thể cảm nhận
A palpable sense of relief spread through the crowd when the rescue succeeded.
obliterate: mark for deletion, rub off, or erase
A UNIVERSAL* DANGER Man’s ability to obliterate life on this planet has increased at a rapid rate.
intersperse with: to scatter or place things at intervals among other things
Lecturers often intersperse with humorous stories their complex academic presentations.
purist: someone who insists on maintaining traditional rules or standards strictly
người theo chủ nghĩa thuần túy
As a culinary purist, she refused to add cream to an authentic Italian carbonara.
kindred spirit: a person whose feelings or attitudes are similar to one's own
người có cùng tâm hồn, tri kỷ
She instantly felt she had met a kindred spirit during their quiet philosophical conversation.
stumble upon: to find or discover something unexpectedly and by chance
tình cờ phát hiện, bắt gặp
Archaeologists managed to stumble upon an intact ancient tomb beneath the crumbling palace.
unflinching: showing determination and courage without hesitating or backing away
The reporter earned great respect for her unflinching determination to expose political corruption.
fade away: The music began to fade away as the train pulled out of the station.
odyssey: a long journey full of adventurous and difficult experiences
hành trình dài đầy gian truân
Their scientific odyssey across Antarctica yielded groundbreaking data about climate change.
serendipitously: happening in an accidental but fortunate and beneficial manner
một cách tình cờ may mắn
The research team serendipitously uncovered a promising cure while investigating a completely different disease.
albeit: The results were encouraging, albeit only in a small pilot study.
stir up: to cause a memory, feeling, or emotion to become active
Old letters can stir up memories you thought had been forgotten.
craftsmanship: skill and care shown in making objects by hand
The carved doors display remarkable craftsmanship and great patience.
moribund: no longer growing or active, and close to the point of failure
The once-thriving industry is now moribund after years of steady decline.
